The actual verifier was inspected and independently rerun: connected labeled cubic graphs on orders four, six, and eight reduce to exactly \(1,2,5\) isomorphism types, and every truncation conflict graph admits a checked six-coloring. The finite domain is exhaustive, not sampled.

value.rationale: The result gives a natural exhaustive finite cutoff for an explicitly open simple-base question, eliminating all smallest connected simple cubic bases and moving any counterexample to order at least ten.
residual_risks: The 19 simple cubic bases on ten vertices and all larger orders remain open.

final_claim: Every connected simple cubic base graph on at most eight vertices has a truncation of strong chromatic index exactly six; hence any counterexample to the simple-base truncation question has at least ten base vertices and at least thirty truncation vertices.
limitations: Finite cutoff only; base order ten and above remain open.
